speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked	the Minister for Finance based on the findings in the Report of the Auditor-General for FY2016/17, whether AGO will direct all the entities in the Report to investigate all improper payments made and determine the amount of money to recover.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The first concerns whether the accounts of the Government are reliable and prepared in accordance with the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The second concerns the rules and procedures in individual public agencies, for example, whether the rules and processes are adequate and have been complied with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In other words, in the AGO’s opinion, the Financial Statements have been presented, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This means that the accounts of the Ministries, departments and Organs of State have all been found to be reliable and prepared in accordance with the law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: AGO noted that the Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE) has recovered the overpaid amounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Economic Development Board (EDB) has completed the remedial action for all payment related lapses, including recovery of monies in the two incidences of overpayments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is also taking corrective actions to make good under-reimbursements and to recover over-reimbursements for the Government-paid Paternity Leave scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) also completed its review of the claims by its agents and service providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: There is no overpayment as the additional sums claimed by its agents have not been paid out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: MOH will only be reimbursing its agents for the correct amount due to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The Government agencies are taking the necessary corrective actions in respect of the lapses highlighted in the AGO report.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have a question because, in the AGO Report, there is also, for example, language used, such as "there is no assurance that the Ministry exercised financial prudence" and also “there is a risk of fraud”.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Can any entity whose lapses are highlighted in the AGO report come to the conclusion that there is no fraud because the AGO report is not forensic in nature?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Png referred to "the Ministry" in his clarification.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One does not go around looking to see whether I can disprove or show that there is no fraud.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It looks at the samples and it considers whether the system as a whole is robust and, if it picks up a point that the system, in itself, has got inefficiencies or deficiencies, it will highlight it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: An audit, by its nature, also, if it encounters a specific lapse or error, such as overpayment or under-reimbursement, it will also highlight that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, what an audit does really is that it does sample checks, sees whether the system as a whole is robust and efficient, and it highlights specific lapses that it may encounter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the nature, not just of an audit by AGO, but of all audits.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Although the AGO or audit is not forensic, so, technically, you cannot detect fraud.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: But in the aftermath of the report, when it was released, MOH, in its statement, said that, "Based on the AGO report, there was no indication of fraud or corrupt practices", which the AGO report did not say.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Then the statement went on to say that "that warrants no further investigation required".

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Would the Senior Minister of State comment on it because I think no one should take the AGO report as an endorsement that there is no fraud.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Like what the Senior Minister of State said, it is selective audit.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: As such, the AGO report, when it came out, the language they used is quite similar to what was also used previously.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: So, no Ministry should take for granted that, because it is not mentioned that there is no fraud, and if there is no fraud, it does not warrant any further investigations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What you have to do is you have to look at the nature of the lapse.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Is it something that requires a further and deep investigation, or is it something that does not?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you can take the statements as reliable.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, the second part of the audit is that you look to see whether or not the rules and processes are adequate and have been complied with.
